nodes.label: Trip State Machine
nodes.rationale: Backend controls all state transitions; the app only triggers actions and listens for events. This decouples client state from server authority.

nodes.label: Clean Architecture (Layers)
nodes.rationale: Three-layer dependency rule (presentation -> domain <- data) allows swapping backend, mappers, or HTTP client without touching UI or viewmodels. Domain is pure Dart, unaware of Flutter.

nodes.label: Vertical Slicing (Feature-Based Structure)
nodes.rationale: Grouping by feature instead of by technical layer makes features autonomous, prevents cross-feature imports, and lets team members work independently.

nodes.label: Screaming Architecture
nodes.rationale: Top-level directory structure reveals the app's domain (auth, profile, rides, documents, vehicle) rather than framework folders like controllers/services.

nodes.label: MVVM Pattern
nodes.rationale: Each feature uses View (Widget), ViewModel (ChangeNotifier), Model (domain entities). View subscribes via context.watch; ViewModel auto-disposes via Riverpod, preventing leaks.

nodes.label: Riverpod Dependency Injection
nodes.rationale: Migrated from legacy provider to Riverpod for better lifecycle management, native auto-dispose providers, and zero widget-tree dependency for DI.

nodes.label: Shared User Entity
nodes.rationale: User is used by auth (creates) and profile (reads/updates). Placing it in shared/ prevents cross-feature imports, preserving vertical slicing autonomy.

nodes.label: Mapper Pattern (Adapter)
nodes.rationale: Domain entities stay pure (no JSON). Serialization lives in dedicated Mapper classes in data/mappers/, so domain never learns about backend format.

nodes.label: Compile-Time Environment Variables (--dart-define-from-file)
nodes.rationale: Chose --dart-define-from-file over flutter_dotenv because flutter_dotenv packages .env as an asset inside APK (readable by anyone), while dart-define injects at compile-time with no plain file left.

nodes.label: JWT in flutter_secure_storage
nodes.rationale: Uses Keystore-level encryption on Android instead of SharedPreferences for token security. AuthStorage interface allows swapping implementations for testing.

nodes.label: Material 3 Theme System
nodes.rationale: Generated via Material Theme Builder from four seed colors. All code references Theme.of(context).colorScheme.X instead of raw hex, giving free dark mode and future palette updates.

nodes.label: FLAG_SECURE (Native Android)
nodes.rationale: Native Kotlin FLAG_SECURE chosen over flutter_windowmanager to avoid extra dependency, activate before Dart code runs, and follow official Android docs.

nodes.label: Navigator 1.0 (Named Routes)
nodes.rationale: Cátedra required Navigator 1.0, not go_router or Navigator 2.0. Routes defined as constants in app_routes.dart.

nodes.label: Typed Exceptions Pattern
nodes.rationale: Chose typed exceptions over Result<T,E> pattern because Dart exceptions with on-catch give the same control with less boilerplate and is more idiomatic.

nodes.label: Single http.Client Instance
nodes.rationale: One http.Client for the whole app avoids multiple connection pools, ensures consistent timeouts/headers, and is disposed via Provider.onDispose.
